target_customer: Engineering teams, from startups to enterprises, wanting automated code review, security scanning and autofix in pull requests
problem: Teams ship bugs and security issues because code review is manual and static analysis tools are noisy and hard to set up.
business_model: B2B SaaS per developer seat with a free tier for open source and a 14 day trial
product_category: Developer tools, static analysis and code review

founders.name: Sanket Saurav
founders.background_notes: From a small town in Bihar, India; company started in Bengaluru per YourStory.

founders.name: Jai Pradeesh
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in press; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building analyzers across many languages with autofix required real compiler and static analysis work but used existing parsers and rule sets.

defensibility.rationale: Rules and integrations are replicable and incumbents like SonarQube, Codacy and GitHub offered scanning; developer experience was the edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platforms added code scanning and AI review; Harness acquired DeepSource in September 2026.

market_need_then: Static analysis was an established category (Codacy, Code Climate, SonarCloud), showing paid demand, and the founders aimed to do for code quality what Travis CI did for CI. Dated 2020 evidence is limited to the founders' stated goal.

branding.domain_note: Uses deepsource.com, exact .com, history not found.

identity.visual_style: Product marketing site with PR comment screenshots and compliance badges
identity.voice_and_tone: Short and confident, tagline 'Your green light to ship with confidence'

branding.brand_signature: Autofix trademark and the green light tagline
branding.community_and_virality: Open source teams adopted it, which a founder called huge validation; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in developer circles and used by thousands of teams, but sources show no distinctive brand asset beyond product quality.

outcome_analysis: DeepSource grew from a developer friendly code analysis tool to an AI code review and security platform trusted by over 7,000 teams per its own page, funded by a $2.6M seed in 2020. It stayed independent for six years in a crowded space and was acquired by Harness in September 2026 to join its autonomous SDLC platform, a strategic exit with no disclosed price.
notes: Pre seed of 140K from angels is mentioned in the seed post but undated, so not recorded as a round. Aggregators give conflicting totals (5.0M, 7.7M, 27.6M); only the 2.6M seed is sourced twice. Competitor search returned only current comparison pages, so the list is empty. YC page says 12 team members and 7,000 plus teams (company claim). Audit fix: the 140K pre-seed from angel investors is stated by the company seed post and by TechCrunch (2020-06-16). The post says Bradley Buda (Founder, Census) wrote the first cheque, and places the round after the February 2019 launch and before the November 2019 YC acceptance; it gives no date, so it is recorded as 2019 (a YourStory snippet says August, not confirmed). Other angels are not named; the earlier note that the round was undated and not recorded is superseded.
